text:
An approval screen can look reassuring. Money needs evidence.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks.

That is the detail I would put in front of business and IT leaders. If a payment can reach execution without passing those checks, the screen tells you less than you hoped.

My concern is the gap between a person approving a payment and the system enforcing that decision. A clear display may help someone make the right call. It does not, by itself, establish that the eventual transfer honours it.

I would ask the business owner and technical owner to trace one approved payment together, all the way to transfer. Identify what the final step checks against the approved amount and recipient, and what stops a mismatch.

The useful evidence is whether the permission survives the journey to where the money moves.
